name: Uyuni Town Center
tagline: The walkable hub around Avenida Ferroviaria
description: The compact heart of town, clustered around Avenida Ferroviaria and the clock tower, where nearly every hostel, tour agency, restaurant, and the bus terminal sit within a few blocks. It is dusty and functional but convenient, and it is where you book tours and refuel between jeep departures.
bestFor: First-time visitors who want everything within walking distance
pros: Everything walkable, from tours to food to buses
Easy to compare and book tour operators
Cheapest concentration of hostels and cafes
cons: Dusty, cold, and short on charm
Quiet and empty once tours depart at dawn

name: Train Cemetery Edge
tagline: Rusting locomotives on the windswept fringe
description: The southwestern edge of town, a short walk or ride from the center, where dozens of rusting antique locomotives sit abandoned on the salt-plain fringe. There is little accommodation out here, but it is an iconic, hauntingly photogenic first or last stop on most salar tours.
bestFor: Photographers and travellers chasing the classic Uyuni shot
pros: One of Uyuni's most photographed sights
Usually the opening stop on jeep tours
cons: No real accommodation or services nearby

name: Colchani
tagline: The salt-processing village at the salar's edge
description: A small village about 20 kilometres north of Uyuni, right where the road meets the salt flat. It is the traditional salt-harvesting and processing community, with artisan salt stalls, souvenir stands, and the first salt hotels. Most tours pause here before rolling out onto the white.
vibe: Rustic salt-country outpost with craft stalls
bestFor: Travellers wanting the salt-village and salar gateway experience
pros: Right at the entrance to the salar
Salt crafts, souvenirs, and salt-block buildings
Closer to the flat than town for sunrise

name: Tahua
tagline: Quiet salar-shore village beneath Tunupa volcano
description: A remote village on the northern shore of the Salar de Uyuni, at the foot of the Tunupa volcano, roughly a couple of hours from town. It offers salt hotels and simple stays for travellers who want to sleep beside the flat, well away from the frontier bustle of Uyuni.
bestFor: Those wanting to overnight on the salar away from town
pros: Direct access to the northern salar
Peaceful salt hotels and clear night skies
cons: Hard to reach without a tour or 4x4
